question: A 2-week-old newborn girl is brought to the physician for a follow-up examination after the initial newborn examination showed asymmetry of the legs. She was born at term to a 26-year-old woman, gravida 3, para 2. Pregnancy was complicated by a breech presentation and treated with an emergency lower-segment transverse cesarean section. The newborn's head circumference is 35 cm (13.7 in). She is at the 60th percentile for length and 75th percentile for weight. Cardiac examination shows no abnormalities. The spine and overlying skin do not indicate significant abnormalities. Abduction of the right hip after cupping the pelvis and flexing the right hip and knee causes a palpable clunk. The feet exhibit no deformities. Ultrasonography of the hip revealed a 50° angle between the lines along the bone acetabulum and the ilium. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.opa: Immobilize the hips with a spica cast
options.opb: Obtain an MRI of the right hip
options.opc: Obtain an X-ray of the right hip
options.opd: Reassure the mother and schedule follow-up appointment in 4 weeks

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Asymmetry of the legs noted -> Possible developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) -> Positive Ortolani sign indicated by palpable clunk -> Ultrasonography shows abnormal hip angle -> Treatment for DDH is indicated -> Harness treatment is a common first-line management -> 85%

CHAIN: Newborn girl with leg asymmetry -> Breech presentation increases risk for hip dysplasia -> Ortolani test positive for right hip -> Ultrasound confirms hip instability -> Spica cast is more invasive than necessary for initial management -> Harness is a less invasive option for treatment -> 90%

CHAIN: 2-week-old newborn with leg asymmetry -> Breech delivery raises suspicion for hip issues -> Positive Ortolani sign suggests hip dysplasia -> Ultrasound shows abnormal hip angle -> Immediate intervention is required -> Harness is a standard treatment for DDH -> 80%

CHAIN: Newborn with leg asymmetry and positive Ortolani sign -> Risk factors include breech presentation -> Ultrasound confirms hip instability -> Spica cast is not first-line for mild cases -> Harness is appropriate for initial management -> 75%
analysis: The newborn girl exhibits signs consistent with developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH), particularly with the positive Ortolani maneuver indicating a dislocated hip that can be reduced. The ultrasound findings suggest hip instability. The most appropriate management for a 2-week-old infant with DDH is to treat using a harness, specifically a Pavlik harness, which is effective in maintaining the hip in a reduced position and promoting proper development of the hip joint. Other options such as immobilization with a spica cast or obtaining an MRI/X-ray are not the first-line management for this age group and condition. Reassurance and follow-up are not appropriate given the findings.
